alerts.title: EFV causing insomnia, vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list persistent central nervous system toxicity, including insomnia and abnormal dreams, as a major adverse event for EFV. The patient reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks, which are classic symptoms of EFV toxicity. No other medications or acute distress are noted that would suggest an alternative cause. The symptoms have persisted, indicating they are not transient initial side effects.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider substituting EFV due to persistent CNS toxicity, as per guideline management for this adverse event.

alerts.title: Viral load monitoring due
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend routine viral load monitoring every one year for adults on ART. The patient's last viral load was on 2025-08-10, which is 165 days (over 5 months) before the current visit. While not yet overdue, the plan does not include scheduling the next annual viral load test. Proactive scheduling ensures continuity of care and timely detection of virologic failure.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load test to align with the guideline of annual monitoring for adults.

alerts.title: Missing annual renal monitoring for TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines specify that for experienced patients on TDF, serum creatinine and eGFR should be done every 12 months as a screening procedure. The patient has been on a TDF-containing regimen since February 2024. There is no record of renal function tests in the provided summary, and the clinician's plan does not include ordering them. Regular monitoring is crucial to detect TDF-associated chronic kidney disease or acute kidney injury early.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR as per guideline for annual monitoring in patients on TDF.
